victim cache: correctness never depends on it
on pressure, the lowest-reuse parked KV moves GPU→GPU,
then →host, then is dropped (§3.3). Parked KV is a victim
cache: the consistency fallback is recompute, so borrowed
memory can always be handed back.
• eviction has exactly one destination — host. UM grows
the very commitment this design sets out to reduce.
• it cannot cross process boundaries, and 2P+2D is four
• it cannot discard: managed pages must be preserved, but
KV may be dropped because recompute is always correct.
The next turn of session S arrives; the prefill node's local radix misses — its prefix was evicted under pressure while the session was in a tool call.
The control plane resolves the prefix hash: the park index says loc = GPU2, and the link table ranks that copy above host DRAM.
Bulk peer-GPU copy GPU2 → GPU0, inserted into the radix as an ordinary prefix hit. No page faults, no host round trip.
Prefill computes only the new tokens and re-parks the extended prefix on whichever GPU is idlest then — host DRAM is never touched.
The cache cannot tell waiting from completed — both are LRU-evictable entries ordered by last access. That is what parking is for.
